title: An etale morphism is smooth with zero-dimensional fibres
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be an etale morphism of schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Then $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and for every $x\in X$, with $s=f(x)$, $\kappa(s)$ its residue field [def-weil-residue-field] and $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ the fibre [def-pc-base-change], the dimension of $X_s$ at the point of $X_s$ corresponding to $x$ is $0$ [def-kun-dimension]. In other words $f$ is smooth of relative dimension zero in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

proof.text: For each x in X, install DiscreteTopology on the scheme-theoretic fibre f.fiber (f x) [def-pc-base-change] using the first conjunct of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points].

Let U be any open neighbourhood of f.asFiber x. The dimension of U is at most that of the ambient discrete fibre, hence at most zero, by Mathlib topologicalKrullDim_subspace_le and topologicalKrullDim_zero_of_discreteTopology. The closure in U of the singleton containing f.asFiber x is nonempty, irreducible and closed, so IrreducibleCloseds U is nonempty and Order.krullDim_nonneg_iff gives dimension at least zero. Thus every such U has dimension exactly zero. Apply topologicalKrullDimAt_eq_of_forall to the infimum in [def-kun-dimension], and assemble the three conjuncts.
